card.name: Words right before "scheduled" in missed doses
card.fires_on: The word just before where "scheduled" or "regularly scheduled" is expected, usually "its" in "take the next dose at its scheduled time" in missed-dose instructions. Also fires on "to" or "usual" in similar phrasing.

modes.label: Missed dose: next dose at its time
modes.description: "its" or "the usual" after "take the next dose at/on" in missed-dose directions.
modes.example: If a dose is missed, take the next dose at<< its>> scheduled time on the following day.

modes.label: Time window before next dose
modes.description: "to" after "prior" in a missed-dose time limit, where timing of the next dose follows.
modes.example: A missed dose can be taken up to 4 hours prior<< to>> the next dose.

modes.label: Scheduler file path
modes.description: A path piece in cron configuration text, apparently where scheduling files are named.

card.writes: It pushes the model to write "schedule" and related forms such as "scheduled" and "scheduling".
card.plain: It fires on the small word before "scheduled" in missed-dose advice like "take the next dose at its scheduled time".
evidence: If a dose is missed, take the next dose at<< its>> scheduled time on the following day.
If a dose is missed by: 3 days or less, take the missed dose as soon as possible, and take the next dose on<< its>> regularly scheduled day.
The next prescribed dose should be taken at the<< usual>> time.
